newsitem.title: JAPAN: FORECAST-Japan May money supply rise seen above 3%.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Japan May money supply rise seen above 3%.

text.p: Japan's money supply growth is likely to have crept up slightly above three percent in May, reflecting a faltering economic recovery and slow growth in bank lending, economists polled by Reuters said on Monday.

The economists gave growth forecasts for Japan's broadly defined money supply average of M2 plus certificates of deposit (M2 plus CDs) ranging from a 2.9 percent increase to a 3.3 percent increase compared with May 1996.
The Bank of Japan will release the data on Wednesday at 0850 JST (2350 GMT, Tuesday). In April, M2 plus CDs grew a preliminary 3.1 percent from a year earlier.

DKB Research said in a report that the government's draining of funds from the private sector and a downdraft in consumer demand following a rush of purchases before an April 1 sales tax increase could keep money supply growth in check.
Postal savings, which are excluded from M2 plus CDs, did not increase in May, and had a neutral impact on money supply growth in that month, the report added.

Mamoru Yamazaki of Paribas Capital Markets predicted a slight increase in the growth rate in May but attributed it largely to a rise in bank deposits. He said there was a fund shift to bank deposits from other financial instruments.
"There is no change in economic fundamentals that would keep boosting money supply growth," he said.
He played down the negative effect of the sales tax increase on money growth.

"We think that the economy will recover later (after a dip in the April-June period), but even so, money supply won't grow rapidly as corporations may continue to shy away from borrowing from banks and try to do business using money at hand," he added.
Yamazaki said the growth rate for M2 plus CDs was basically expected to drift between 3.0 and 4.0 percent in the near term, with an occasional dip below 3.0 percent.
